title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (Nov 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates the current product overview, PRD-level requirements, design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for Redwood Inference's Unified Inference product family as of Nov 2026. It is intended for product, engineering, go-to-market, and customer-facing teams preparing launches, sales enablement, and customer migrations.

Executive summary
- Goal: Provide a single, consistent inference API and operational experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments that optimizes for latency, cost, and reliability.
- Primary customer persona: ML engineers and platform engineers at scale-ups and enterprises needing predictable inference economics and enterprise controls.
- Success metrics (Q4 2026 target): +30% self-serve activation conversion, 20% reduction in median per-token cost for targeted workloads using Optimize recommendations, 99.95% per-route availability for SLA tiers.

Product overview & positioning
- What it is:
  - Unified inference API (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking).
  - Runtime optimizations (KV/prefix cache, batching, kernel selection, quantization profiles).
  - Operational features (per-route dashboards, cost/latency breakdowns, rollouts, canaries, automatic fallbacks).
- Differentiators:
  1) Production-first operational tooling integrated with the API.
  2) Cost-aware routing and model variant fallbacks.
  3) Seamless parity of features between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

Product Requirements (PRD) - high level
1) Core API parity (MUST)
   - REST + gRPC endpoints for: generate, chat, embeddings, rerank, model-info.
   - Streaming support for generate/chat with chunked tokens and backpressure.
   - Per-request metadata: customer_id, route_id, priority (low/standard/high), cost_profile_hint.
   - Auth: API keys + mTLS for Private deployments.
2) Performance & cost controls (MUST)
   - Per-route SLO config: p50/p95/p99 latency SLOs, throughput targets, max-burst tokens.
   - Autoscaling integration for Dedicated pools and alerting thresholds.
   - Intelligent batching and KV caching enabled by default with opt-out flags.
3) Model variants & fallbacks (SHOULD)
   - Model catalog entries must include performance profile (latency/cost/quality tradeoffs).
   - Smart routing policy engine to select by latency/cost/region/tier and to execute fallback to compatible variants when primary not available.
4) Rollouts & experiments (SHOULD)
   - Canary and A/B rollout primitives with percentage controls and automatic rollback on defined quality regressions.
   - Integration with Redwood Optimize to automatically propose rollout weights.
5) Observability & cost attribution (MUST)
   - Token-level cost breakdown for requests.
   - Per-route/model dashboards with 90-day retention (configurable for enterprise).
   - Tracing hooks compatible with OpenTelemetry.
6) Security & compliance (MUST for Private)
   - Support for KMS integrations (Customer-managed keys), audit logging, RBAC, and HIPAA/PCI evidence package templates.

Design specifications (selected components)
- API contract (abridged)
  - POST /v1/generate
    - request: { model: string, prompt: string | array, max_tokens: int, temperature: float, route_id: string, metadata: map }
    - response stream: token events, token_index, partial_text, finish_reason
  - Error model: standard 4xx/5xx with structured error code, retriable boolean, and suggested fallback_model field.

- Routing & policy engine
  - Inputs: route_id, customer tier, region, latency_budget_ms, cost_target_usd_per_1k_tokens, model_compatibility_list.
  - Output: selected_model, quantization_variant, execution_cluster, estimated_cost_per_token.
  - Policy rules (examples):
    1) If latency_budget_ms < 100 AND dedicated_capacity_available -> prefer low-latency float16 models.
    2) If cost_target < baseline AND model supports 4-bit quantization -> prefer quantized variant and enable batching.

- Batching & cache model
  - Continuous batching window: dynamic between 4\u201330ms depending on incoming qps and latency SLO.
  - KV cache scope: per-customer per-model session scope with TTL (default 24h).
  - Cache policies: prefix-based lookup, cache hit bypass for privacy-sensitive requests (flagged).

- Rollout / Release mechanics
  1) Create release candidate (RC) branch + model artifact pinned in catalog.
  2) Internal smoke tests: perf bench, unit eval, security checks.
  3) Canary release to 2% of traffic for 24h, with automated quality/regression checks on eval prompts and SLA metrics.
  4) Gradual ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 72\u2013168h with health gates.
  5) Rollback plan: automatic rollback on >5% QoR (quality) regression or >2x error rate increase vs baseline.

Roadmap & themes (Q1 2027 through Q3 2027)
- Theme A: \u201ePredictable Economics\u201c (Q1\u2013Q2 2027)
  - Feature: Optimize recommendations v3 (workload-specific quantization + caching profiles).
  - Metric: 15\u201330% unit cost reduction on benchmarked workloads.
- Theme B: "Enterprise Hardening" (Q2 2027)
  - Feature: Private deployment automated installers, expanded KMS/HSM drivers, longer audit retention options.
  - Metric: 3 signed Private contracts (>$250k ARR) by EOY.
- Theme C: "Developer Velocity & Observability" (Q2\u2013Q3 2027)
  - Feature: Per-route SLO templates, richer tracing, cost attribution export to Snowflake.
  - Metric: NPS for developer experience > 65.
- Milestones (planned)
  - 2026-12-15: GA release of Unified Inference v2026.4 (hosted + dedicated feature parity for core API).
  - 2027-03-31: Redwood Optimize v3 + integrated rollout suggestions.
  - 2027-06-30: Private deployment automated installer (v1), expanded compliance package.

Pricing & packaging notes
- Product tiers (high level)
  1) Starter (self-serve hosted)
     - Target: developers, prototypes.
     - Pricing: $0.02 per 1k generation tokens, $0.10 per 1k embedding units (intro).
     - Limits: 60 req/min route default, 7-day observability retention.
  2) Scale (hosted + Dedicated BY request)
     - Target: scaleups, mid-market.
     - Pricing: tiered per-token with volume discounts (example: $0.015 -> $0.008 per 1k tokens depending on usage), dedicated capacity add-on pricing by GPU-pool size.
     - Features: 30-day retention, per-route SLOs, dedicated support channel.
  3) Enterprise (Dedicated & Private)
     - Target: regulated customers and high-throughput deployments.
     - Pricing: committed capacity contracts + platform fee. Example: $X/month per reserved GPU with % discount for annual commit.
     - Features: 90-day+ observability retention, KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2/HIPAA evidence, custom SLAs.
- Packaging notes & sell motion
  - Optimize upsell: Recommend Optimize for customers with >$5k/mo spend; bundle first month of Optimize insights for new Scale customers.
  - Dedicated packaging: provide 3, 6, 12 month reserved capacity agreements; include burst credits for first month.
  - Private packaging: fixed onboarding fee + annual platform license + optional managed services.

Release notes (latest RC: 2026.11.25-rc1)
- High level: Consolidated runtime improvements and new rollout gating for quality-driven automatic rollback.
- Highlights:
  - Runtime: improved kernel selection reduced p95 latency by ~12% on Llama-family models (internal perf bench v2026.11).
  - Routing: added cost_target policy in routing engine and UI support to set per-route cost targets.
  - Rollouts: automated quality gating using eval prompt sets with configurable thresholds.
  - Observability: token-level cost export to S3 + Snowflake connector (beta).
  - Security: new KMS provider adapter for CloudVendorX and additional audit log fields for Private deployments.
- Known issues:
  1) Canaries for dedicated GPU pools may report inflated error rates for the first 30 minutes due to pool warm-up. Mitigation: extend canary window by 30m for GPU-backed routes.
  2) Cache TTL mismatch between catalog and runtime where TTL updates are delayed for 2\u20135 minutes during rollout. Future fix: synchronize catalog writes via a single CDC pipeline.

Operational readiness checklist (pre-GA)
- Ownership: Release owner: Aisha Patel (Product); Tech lead: Miguel Fernandez (Eng - serving runtime); SRE lead: Priya Ramesh.
- Tests: perf bench results uploaded (artifact id: perf/2026.11.20), regression evals run against canonical prompt sets (pass rate >= 98%), security scan clearance.
- Docs & enablement: API docs updated, SDK release notes drafted, sales playbook & pricing cheat sheet completed.
- Support: runbook for rollout rollback and incident response published at /eng-platform/runbooks/unified-inference-rollout.json.

Open risks & mitigation
- Risk: Model quality regressions when applying aggressive quantization.
  - Mitigation: gated rollout with automatic quality checks and Canary evaluation sets plus manual QA for top 10 customers.
- Risk: Customers misconfigure per-route cost targets causing unexpected throttling.
  - Mitigation: UI warnings, default safe lower bounds, and an override path requiring >1 engineer approval for enterprise tenants.

Appendix: Example SLO table (per-route)
| SLO name | p50 | p95 | p99 | error budget/day | notes |
|----------|-----|-----|-----|------------------|-------|
| Serve-standard | 45ms | 120ms | 350ms | 0.05% | Default for hosted standard tier |
| Serve-low-latency | 12ms | 45ms | 120ms | 0.01% | Reserved for Dedicated low-latency pools |

Appendix: rollout CLI examples
1) Create a canary rollout (example):
$ redwood rollout create --route onboarding-chat --model rwd/llama-13b-fp16 --percent 2 --duration 24h --health-gates eval_set=onboarding-prompts:95
2) Promote canary to 25%:
$ redwood rollout promote --id rc-2026-11-25-01 --to 25
